definitions.explanation: A piece of gymnastics equipment consisting of stacked rectangular sections that athletes run up to and vault over. A staple of Japanese school physical education.

examples.japanese: {八|はち}{段|だん}の{跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}が{跳|と}べるようになった。
examples.english: I became able to vault over an eight-level box.

examples.japanese: {小学校|しょうがっこう}の{体育|たいいく}で{跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}が{苦手|にがて}だった{思|おも}い{出|で}がある。
examples.english: I have memories of being bad at the vaulting box in elementary school gym class.

notes:
Composed of {跳|と}び (jumping) + {箱|ばこ} (box). A quintessential piece of Japanese school gym equipment. The box consists of stacked trapezoidal sections (typically 5-8 levels), and students run up to it, push off a springboard, and vault over it. The height is adjusted by adding or removing sections.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}を{跳|と}ぶ: to vault over the box
- {跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}{八|はち}{段|だん}: eight-level vaulting box
- {跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}が{得意|とくい}: to be good at vaulting
- {跳|と}び{箱|ばこ}が{苦手|にがて}: to be bad at vaulting

TECHNIQUES:
- {開脚|かいきゃく}{跳|と}び: straddle vault (legs apart)
- {閉脚|へいきゃく}{跳|と}び: squat vault (legs together)
- {台上|だいじょう}{前転|ぜんてん}: forward roll on top of the box

CULTURAL NOTE:
The {跳|と}び{箱|ばこ} is a nearly universal experience in Japanese physical education. Being able to clear a high number of levels is a source of pride for children.
